title: Al-'Asr again: the four
hook: Imam al-Shafi'i said this surah alone would be enough guidance

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-'Asr, the oath by time and the verdict of loss. Your line was by time. Did you spend five minutes well, on purpose? What did you choose? Day one hundred seventy-two.

If you could keep only one page of advice for the rest of your life, what would be on it? People argue about this over dinner: one book, one verse, one sentence. Imam al-Shafi'i, one of the great scholars of Islamic law, who lived about twelve hundred years ago and founded one of the four Sunni schools, had an answer about the Qur'an. He's reported to have said that if people reflected on this one surah, it would be enough for them. Three lines. Today: Al-'Asr again, the four.
screen: `ONE PAGE FOR THE REST OF YOUR LIFE.` → `IMAM AL-SHAFI'I.` → `IT WOULD BE ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: Yesterday: by time, the human being is in loss. Today, the exception, in Pickthall's words: Save those who believe and do good works, and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance. Four things. First, faith: iman, trust in Allah, the root under everything else. Second, good deeds: 'amal salih, faith that turns into hands. Scholars note the Qur'an pairs these two dozens of times; one without the other is incomplete. Now the surprise. The last two are not things you do alone. The Arabic word is tawasaw: urge one another, counsel each other, a verb that only works between people. Urge one another to truth, al-haqq: what's right, what's real, even when it's awkward to say. And urge one another to patience, as-sabr: endurance, holding steady, not giving up on the right thing when it gets hard. So the way out of loss isn't a private self-improvement plan. It's a small community of people who keep each other honest and keep each other going. It's reported that when two companions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ met, they wouldn't part until one of them had recited this surah to the other. That's what al-Shafi'i saw in it. Belief, action, and two kinds of friendship: the friend who tells you the truth, and the friend who helps you stay the course. Faith, good, truth, patience. Most people can name who in their life gives them each one.
screen: `IMAN — FAITH.` · `'AMAL SALIH — GOOD DEEDS.` · `TAWASAW — URGE ONE ANOTHER.` · `TO TRUTH, AND TO PATIENCE.` · then, large: `FAITH, GOOD, TRUTH, PATIENCE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: name the four in your life. Sit, and take them one at a time, a breath for each. Faith: where does your trust rest right now? Good: one thing you did this week that helped someone. Truth: who tells you the truth, even when it's hard to hear? Patience: who helps you keep going? Let a face come for each one. If a place is empty, just notice it. The bell holds the time.
Al-'Asr again. The four that keep a person from loss: faith, good deeds, urging one another to truth, and to patience. Today's word.
Your line: faith, good, truth, patience. Today, be one of the four for someone else. Tell a friend a kind truth, or help them hold on to something hard. Day one hundred seventy-two.

howItsDone: Many Muslims know al-'Asr by heart and recite it in the prayers; teachers often use it as a summary of Islamic life, and some friends end a gathering by reciting it together.

fork.setup: two companions of the Prophet meet on the road and talk. before they part, what is it reported they did?
options: one recited Surah al-'Asr to the other
fork.reveal: it's reported they wouldn't part until one recited al-'Asr to the other: a reminder of the four, between friends.

original.note: Arabic: they urged one another, counseled each other; the verb of 103:3.

trapdoor: what you thought: a list of four virtues.
what it means: faith and good deeds, plus two things done together: urging one another to truth and to patience.
what a scholar hears: tawasaw is reciprocal; al-Shafi'i's saying is reported by Ibn Kathir; the companions' custom is in al-Tabarani, with a chain some scholars question.
